_note: Finding ids frozen on 2026-11-18 BEFORE any validator or converter code. Severity: error = the rule is invalid or cannot work as written; warning = probably a mistake; info = quality advice. All rules and examples are written by CyberDat; no SigmaHQ rule (DRL 1.1) is included.

sigma.meaning: YAML anchors, aliases, tags or merge keys are not accepted
title missing or not a string
logsource missing or without category, product or service
detection missing or not a mapping
date or modified not in YYYY-MM-DD
level not one of informational, low, medium, high, critical
status not one of stable, test, experimental, deprecated, unsupported
tag not in a known namespace format (attack.*, cve.*, car.*, tlp.*, detection.*)
condition refers to a search identifier that does not exist
search identifier never used by the condition
overly broad value (only wildcards, or contains/startswith/endswith with fewer than 3 characters)
duplicate value or duplicate search identifier content

yara.meaning: invalid or reserved rule name or tag
invalid regular expression (static check, never executed)
unknown or invalid string modifier for the string type
module used in the condition but not imported
meta value is not a string, integer or boolean
regular expression likely slow (leading or unbounded .* / .+, nested quantifiers)
condition has no file size limit

conversion: Targets: Splunk SPL (search expression), Microsoft KQL (where expression), Elastic Lucene (query string). Supported: field/value maps (AND), value lists (OR), keyword lists, modifiers contains, startswith, endswith, all, exists, re (KQL and Lucene only), cidr (KQL and Lucene only), null values, numbers, wildcards * (all) and ? (Lucene only), conditions with and, or, not, parentheses, 1 of / all of with patterns or them. Anything else gives an error naming the construct. Output format: operators AND/OR/NOT (SPL, Lucene) or and/or/not() (KQL); parentheses only where precedence needs them; values in NFC.
